correctness.rationale: Direct planar convex-geometry reconstruction gives the exact two facet lengths and atom masses. The support signs, active interval, scaling exponent, \(p=2\) degeneracy, critical-point equation, threshold \(p_*\), and one/two/three root counts were checked symbolically and against the packaged numerical consistency tests. The proof of the all-parameter statement is analytic; finite tests are not used as exhaustive evidence.

evidence: Ai–Ye–Zhu Theorem 3.1 gives existence and uniqueness for all nonzero finite measures when \(0\le p\le1\), without an explicit atomic inverse.
Yang–Ye–Zhu Theorem 6.2 gives compact-support exact existence for \(p\ne0,n\) and uniqueness for \(0<p<1\), but no multiplicity classification for \(p>1\).
Schneider explicitly discusses one-point support for ordinary surface area measure, not interacting two-atom \(L_p\) data.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader existence theorems do not imply the explicit number of solutions outside their uniqueness range, nor the sharp threshold or \(p=2\) compatibility curve. Conversely the present finding is deliberately narrower and does not claim to improve general existence.

evidence: The 2022 theorem stops uniqueness at \(0<p<1\) and excludes \(p=n\) from exact scaling; therefore it does not imply the \(p>p_*\) triple-solution regime or the \(p=2\) compatibility family.
The 2026 theorem gives uniqueness for \(0\le p\le1\) and contains no explicit two-atom inverse.
Khovanskiĭ–Timorin show support-number linearity and area quadraticity in planar coconvex polygons, but do not formulate the \(L_p\) measure inversion.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new claim is not obtained by simply specializing a stronger theorem: the multiplicity analysis requires the exact two-facet mass map and its critical-point structure, which the inspected general results do not supply.

evidence: The semantic-database searches returned no record whose statement reduces two-atom planar \(C\)-close \(L_p\) data to the same scalar map \(\Phi_p\) or gives the same threshold \(p_*\).
The inspected primary and supporting literature contains general existence theorems and support-number geometry, but no identical one/two/three-solution phase diagram.

originality.rationale: The inspected literature establishes general existence/continuity or support-number frameworks but does not state the exact two-atom scalar inverse, the \(p=2\) compatibility curve, or the geometry-dependent multiplicity threshold. Targeted database and literature searches found no equivalent claim; the remaining risk is an unindexed elementary calculation.
residual_risks: An equivalent elementary two-facet calculation could exist in an unindexed thesis, note, or non-English source.

The global statement that two-atom planar data force exactly two interior facets relies on the standard monotone-Gauss-angle structure of planar convex boundaries; no higher-dimensional analogue is asserted.

value.rationale: Two atoms form the first interacting discrete case after the known one-point model. The result is a complete natural classification: explicit inversion in the recently solved \(0\le p\le1\) regime, exact critical homogeneity at \(p=2\), and a sharp geometry-dependent transition to three solutions for large \(p\). It is useful as a benchmark for discrete Minkowski solvers and for understanding where general uniqueness can fail.
